verified: Reuters, citing internal memos it reviewed, reported that Microsoft declared a "Code Red" drive to overhaul how it prevents and responds to major service failures after the November 12 outage, and quoted Microsoft 365 Core President Jason Henderson calling it the most customer-impacting incident in Exchange Online's history. Microsoft's own post-incident report, dated November 20, traced the disruption to an undetected Windows scalability defect introduced in July that caused lock contention in gateway processes, worsened by a Teams traffic failover and maintenance that had left nearly 14 percent of gateway server capacity offline.
unconfirmed: Microsoft has not published the memos or publicly confirmed the "Code Red" program or its targets — including the stated goal of moving an urgent fix from detection to safe worldwide deployment within one hour, which Henderson is quoted as saying the company has not reached ("we aren't here yet"), and the reported five to six days a recent urgent production fix took to reach worldwide saturation. Those figures and the characterization of the outage's record severity rest on Reuters' review of internal documents rather than an on-the-record Microsoft statement, and the memos do not set out a timeline or completion criteria for the overhaul.

titles.en: Microsoft declares internal 'Code Red' after Exchange Online outage
